findings.text: follow-on: the plan §3 done-when has three clauses and the node's evidence fragment carries none of the measured ones. §3 requires 'a cold fetch of one OP2 shot's first-pass signals completes through the extractor in a single ssh session; a warm read of the same signals through the view touches no network; and the extractor's wall time per signal and bytes per signal are recorded in the evidence'. The delivered fragment states only that the code exists. The single-ssh-session and no-network-on-warm-read properties are asserted against a fake transport (tests/data/test_eddb_cache.py::test_one_transport_process_per_batch and ::test_a_cached_channel_causes_no_transport_call), which is legitimate for a unit gate, but the wall-time-per-signal and bytes-per-signal measurement — the clause whose stated purpose is 'so the cache for a shot set is sized rather than guessed' — is absent, and no real cold fetch was run (the ssh link to IFERC dropped; plan §5). The node's manifest does not list this as a follow-on, so a reader of the landing record would take §3's measurement clause as satisfied when it is not. The follow-on is to run one real OP2 cold fetch on the healthy link and record seconds and bytes per signal in the evidence.

follow-on, flagged by the node and confirmed here: the cache directory is named by the raw EDDB shot token ('{shot}.zarr') while ZarrTransformEngine/VirtualZarrView open a pulse as f"{int(shot)}.zarr". The integration test test_cached_store_opens_through_engine_and_view_with_no_transport_call uses shot='51234', which is int-convertible, so it never exercises the case the plan says is live — §3 records that 'the current shot is a coil-commissioning pulse (C-series)'. A C-series or E-series token is not int-convertible, so the cache's headline property (readable by the existing engine with no new reader) does not hold for the shot class in use. The node records this in evidence_inputs and as a follow-on; it is out of this node's code scope, but it is the gap between the delivered layout and the section's real read path.

follow-on: REMOTE_SCRIPT, the half of the extractor that actually calls eddbreadTime/eddbreadOne against libeddb, is never executed by any test. test_the_remote_script_uses_stdlib_numpy_and_the_wrapper_only only substring-matches the source text ('eddb_pwrapper' in REMOTE_SCRIPT, 'import requests' not in REMOTE_SCRIPT). The client-side envelope is round-tripped in-process (test_envelope_round_trips_through_encode_and_decode) but the remote producer of that same envelope is unverified, so the equivalence the module docstring claims ('the client decodes both identically') rests on inspection alone. Unreachable from a test by design; the follow-on is a one-shot smoke run of the script against the analysis server on a healthy link, comparing its bytes to encode_batch's for a known record.

follow-on, evidence integrity: the reviewed run's negative_control_note names the mutation as '(create_array overwrite=True)', but that change alone does not disable the overwrite guard. The guard is the explicit membership test 'if record.dname in category: raise EddbCacheError(...)' at eddb.py:82-87, which fires before create_array is reached. Reproduced this review: a head tree with only create_array(overwrite=True) applied still passes the gate 10/10 (negative-control.log, EXIT=0); a head tree with the membership guard removed fails exactly test_writing_over_an_existing_channel_is_refused with 'DID NOT RAISE EddbCacheError' (negative-control-2.log, EXIT=1), matching the node's own red log. So the guard is real and falsifiable, but the note misdescribes the mutation a reproducer must apply; the note should name the membership check.

follow-on (minor): is_cached() returns False when the on-disk path exists but does not open as a zarr array (KeyError/ValueError/OSError), while write_channel() then raises EddbCacheError because the name is present in the group. The two predicates disagree for a path that exists but is unreadable or is a group rather than an array: fetch_channels would treat the channel as missing, call the transport, and then write_channel would refuse, so the batch fetch is spent before the refusal. Single-writer and normally consistent, so no test exercises it; a corrupt or half-written channel is the only path there. No action required for this node; noted for the next reader.
